title: Cushion Months in Flood Refund Reviews When the Home Is No Longer Occupied
content:
Where a Summit Tax and Insurance Reserve under Set-Aside Accounts reviews a returned flood premium, the flood refund need carries a cushion measured in months of charges when the Summit loan's occupancy profile (Occupancy and Residency Certification) and maturity case (Maturity and Due-and-Payable Cases) show the home is no longer occupied by the borrower. A month of charges is the annual property tax plus the annual hazard premium plus the annual flood premium on file, divided by twelve.

**Points of judgement**

1. *Is the occupancy profile of the reserve's Summit loan closed, and is the loan's maturity case a Death of Last Surviving Borrower case that is due and payable or in its extension period?* If so, the flood refund cushion is the estate cushion months, 3, times a month of charges.
2. *Otherwise, does the occupancy profile show non-occupancy confirmed, with an occupancy inspection ordered on it within the twelve months before the handling date* (an inspection order dated no later than the handling date and fewer than 12 whole calendar months before it)? If so, the flood refund cushion is the moved-out cushion months, 1, times a month of charges.
3. If neither holds, this rule adds no cushion.

**Hypothetical figures.** On file: tax 2,400.00, hazard 1,200.00, flood 720.00, so a month of charges is 360.00. The estate cushion is 1,080.00; the moved-out cushion is 360.00. A profile showing non-occupancy confirmed whose only inspection order is 14 months old gives no cushion under this rule.
